paper.title: Mobility promotes and jeopardizes biodiversity in rock-paper-scissors games

headline: Spatial rock-paper-scissors (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; spatial #surviving=3.0 (coexist 100%) vs well-mixed #surviving=1.0 (biodiversity lost)

verdicts.gate: P1 spatial coexistence (all 3 species fraction > 0.05 in >=80% of seeds)
P2 well-mixed loses biodiversity (>=1 species extinct; max #surviving < 3)

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the spatial-coexistence vs well-mixed-extinction result and would catch an artifact

citations: Reichenbach, T., Mobilia, M. & Frey, E. (2007). Mobility promotes and jeopardizes biodiversity in rock-paper-scissors games. Nature 448:1046-1049. doi:10.1038/nature06095.
Reichenbach, T., Mobilia, M. & Frey, E. (2008). Self-organization of mobile populations in cyclic competition. J. Theor. Biol. 254(2):368-383. doi:10.1016/j.jtbi.2008.05.014.
May, R.M. & Leonard, W.J. (1975). Nonlinear aspects of competition between three species. SIAM J. Appl. Math. 29(2):243-253. doi:10.1137/0129022.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction
